source.licence_name: FSANZ Data User Licence Agreement based on Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0 Australia

official_terms_observed.acceptance_language: The FSANZ page says to read and accept the terms before downloading files, and that exercising granted rights constitutes acceptance.
official_terms_observed.derivative_work_boundary: Editing, modifying or adapting the Work or a substantial part may be a Derivative Work; whether one food row or selected nutrient cells meet this threshold is not resolved by the text alone.
distribution_conditions: Provide the licence URI or a copy with distributed Work.
Include the Limitation of Data Statement and a notice that Australian data may not be appropriate for other countries with every copy of distributed Work.
Preserve copyright and disclaimer notices and provide attribution in a manner reasonable to the medium.
Do not impose terms or technological measures on the Work that prevent recipients from exercising the licence rights.
official_terms_observed.share_alike_boundary: A distributed Derivative Work must use the licence; the agreement says this does not require other independent material in a Collection or the Collection as a whole to use that licence.
official_terms_observed.third_party_data_notice: The AFCD contains third-party data and material; FSANZ says it makes no warranty that reuse will not infringe third-party rights.

project_application_analysis.public_app: The agreement grants worldwide, royalty-free rights subject to its terms and does not state a non-commercial-only restriction. This does not by itself establish that this project's exact use is cleared.
project_application_analysis.sqlite_persistence: If stored material is a copy of protected Work, digital storage falls within the agreement's definition of reproduction. Applicability to an extracted single-record nutrient profile remains unresolved.
project_application_analysis.api_or_ui_delivery: If a response contains licensed Work or a Derivative Work, public electronic delivery appears within the agreement's distribution definition; exact treatment of selected facts and normalized profiles needs written clarification.
project_application_analysis.model_extracted_profile: Converting source cells into the application's fixed schema may be a transformation, but whether the selected fields constitute a substantial part or derivative is unresolved. Model use does not independently grant rights.
project_application_analysis.application_code_license: The agreement says other independent material in a Collection and the Collection as a whole need not be relicensed solely because it contains the Work or a Derivative Work. It remains unresolved whether the proposed profile is a separate Derivative Work or only a Collection item.
project_application_analysis.third_party_rights: The record-level third-party source lineage and any relevant exceptions have not been independently cleared.

decision.reason: The licence provides a possible reuse path with concrete conditions, but the status of a selected F001301 profile, durable SQLite copies, public API/UI delivery, model-normalized derivatives and third-party lineage is not sufficiently clear to admit the source.

publisher_questions_before_admission: For a public, free, non-commercial university project, may the app retain one AFCD food record's selected nutrient values and source provenance durably in SQLite, including user-specific profile or meal snapshots and backups?

May the server return those selected values to app users through an authenticated API and display them in a nutrition preview, and what exact attribution, licence link, data limitation and Australian-data notice must accompany each response, screen, export or saved copy?

Does extracting selected nutrient cells from the F001301 public detail page or file and mapping them into a fixed JSON nutrition schema count as a Derivative Work or substantial part under the FSANZ agreement? If so, should only the profile/data artifact be licensed CC BY-SA 3.0 AU, or does FSANZ consider any additional part of the app affected?
Does the answer differ between copying values from the public detail page, downloading the AFCD files after acceptance, and having Tavily/model tooling retrieve and normalize the page?
Does the agreement cover all third-party-derived components in F001301 for this use, or must the project separately clear any record-level source material?
next_gate: Obtain written FSANZ clarification on the exact durable storage, public delivery and model-normalized profile workflow; do not accept the licence or download the dataset on the user's behalf.

If the publisher confirms the path, have the project owner review and accept the applicable terms, then design attribution and notices at API, UI, export and persisted-copy boundaries before admission.
Separately define analytical, source-derived, imputed-zero and missing-value semantics without copying real nutrient values into a test fixture before reuse is cleared.
Only after the rights gate, run a bounded single-source format/adapter test; label it source-format testing, not photo-pipeline or nutrition-accuracy validation.
Keep F001301 limited to an explicitly labelled raw per-100-g reference until a reviewed raw-equivalent portion conversion exists.
review_limits: This is a technical reading of published terms, not legal advice or a legal determination.
A public webpage review is not dataset download, licence acceptance or permission to reuse data.
The terms' definition of substantial part does not resolve whether one record or selected nutrient facts are protected or derivative.
The licence's third-party-data caveat leaves record-level source lineage as a separate risk.
No real F001301 nutrient values were copied into this evidence artifact.
